content.title: Rapper returned to custody months after early prison release
content.text: NewsRapper Pooh Shiesty is back in custody in Dallas, Texas, months after his early release from federal prison as hip‑hop fans watch his legal situation closely.Paras Griffin/Getty ImagesDALLAS — Rapper Pooh Shiesty was arrested in Dallas, Texas, three months after he was released early from federal prison, according to public records and published reports Monday. The news has surprised fans as the Memphis artist had only recently begun working on new music and rebuilding his career. Pooh Shiesty’s real name is Lontrell Donell Williams Jr. He first rose to fame with songs like Back in Blood and was signed to Gucci Mane’s 1017 label before his legal problems. The rapper had been serving a federal sentence for a firearms conspiracy charge related to a 2020 crime in Florida. Although his original release date was set for April 2026, federal prison records show he was freed early in October 2025 after about three years behind bars. Just weeks after his release, Pooh Shiesty dropped new music, including a track called FDO, which stands for ‘First Day Out,’ that celebrated his return and featured shout outs to other hip‑hop artists. The Federal Bureau of Prisons records now show the rapper is back in custody at the Residential Reentry Management (RRM) facility in Dallas, and his new release date has been listed as April 11, 2026. Officials have not yet provided details about the reason for this recent arrest or what charges, if any, he may be facing. The arrest has drawn attention from fans and media because Pooh Shiesty was widely expected to continue his comeback after prison. Many observers had been watching his early career return closely, especially after he released FDO and began engaging with followers on social media. At age 26, Pooh Shiesty became one of the more high‑profile rappers to be released early from prison, and his early freedom had generated hope among fans that he could continue building his music career. His song FDO even reached the charts late last year.So far, neither the Dallas Police Department nor the rapper’s legal team have released a public statement about the latest arrest. It is also not clear whether the arrest is related to probation issues, new charges or a federal hold. In an earlier video shared online, Pooh Shiesty also showed paperwork from his past federal case and denied rumors that he cooperated with authorities, saying he stayed strong through his legal troubles.
